name: Emperors of Rome: From Augustus to Justinian
description: Twenty-odd emperors, good and bad, who ran the largest state of the ancient world, and the generals, orators and rebels who shaped their age.

checkpoints.name: The Republic falls
checkpoints.note: Rome's old republic breaks under civil war. Caesar crosses the Rubicon and is murdered, and his heir Octavian becomes Augustus, the first emperor.

checkpoints.name: Julio-Claudian emperors
checkpoints.note: The family of Augustus holds the throne. Tiberius, Caligula, Claudius and Nero rule from Rome, with court plots, conquest in Britain and the great fire of Rome.

checkpoints.name: Flavians and the good emperors
checkpoints.note: After a year of civil war, Vespasian founds a new line and the Colosseum rises; Vesuvius buries Pompeii in 79. A run of capable emperors from Nerva to Marcus Aurelius, among them Hadrian with his wall and the Pantheon, takes the empire to its widest reach and its calmest years.

checkpoints.name: Severans and crisis
checkpoints.note: Commodus is killed, soldiers make and unmake emperors, and Septimius Severus and Caracalla rely on the army while invasions and the Plague of Cyprian strain the state.

checkpoints.name: A Christian empire
checkpoints.note: Diocletian splits the government, Constantine founds Constantinople and favours Christianity, and Theodosius makes it the state faith. Rome is sacked in 410 and Attila threatens the West, which falls in 476, while Justinian rules the Byzantine Empire from the East.
